utterances.text: It's not a videotape. It's an audiotape.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: How do you know he's got it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Because in the presence of the lawyer, Azem Mehonjic, he called me and asked that I only tell the truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, are you saying that you've spoken to Mr. Delalic about these proceedings or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: We didn't talk about the trial. He merely told me to say the things as they were, so just to tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And as to this tape, have you told the Prosecution about the existence of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Which person did you tell about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I told someone here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Who was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Who? It was during the proofing that I told Mr. Brun, because I asked him whether I could bring money as evidence for my testimony and he said that this was not a good idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you tell any of the people present in court today during the course of your proofing notes, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, you've had a proofing -- in fact, you've had three proofing sessions with you, have you not, with Ms. Chana who's present here and led you in your evidence in chief; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No, that's not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, have you had two sessions with her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: It's not right. It's not true that I had three preparations. I've had one. I arrived on the 15th. I had two proofing sessions. One lasted several hours, and the second one was not even a proofing session but it had to do with the threats against me prior to my arrival here from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And did you tell --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, well, well, Mr. Morrissey, I have to warn you at this stage that this witness is a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, this -- letting out the witness's name has happened now on, I think, at least six -- six occasions. I'd like to believe it's inadvertent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, usually we don't -- we do everything possible to send signals to the parties as a warning. We do not have it in the transcript, you know, because we need some redactions also to that effect. And I believe that Mr. Morrissey in the future will take our warnings seriously.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I indicate I do take them very seriously. And you will have seen how this has unfolded for a number of witnesses now. I am sorry that it's -- but it's happened this way. And we'll endeavour to do better.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But now that that issue is over with, could we come back to this. You see Ms. Chana sitting over there. Did you tell her about this tape or didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember really. But I -- I've asked to be a protected witness here. You've -- you've kept mentioning my name. But no matter. You are defending a person here who knows about the events in Grabovica. You're merely trying to do your job, to have your own case out --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I don't want to know about my role. Thanks. What I want to put -- I'll put a more general proposition and then we're going to start at the start. And the more general proposition is this: You and Ramiz Delalic -- I'll put it another way. Ramiz Delalic through his agent, you, is putting material before this Court with the sole view of distracting attention from the 9th Brigade killers and focussing it on the accused, Mr. Halilovic. Do you agree with that proposition or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object to this question on the grounds it's speculating as to what Ramiz Delalic is doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's not a proper question, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you can -- if you reconsider the question on the transcript there, I submit I'm entitled -- I have to put it to this witness because I'm putting a collusion. I've got to put that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that in this situation, you have to build up your case step by step, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's true, but it's -- but it is cross-examination. However, Your Honour, I hear what you say. I'll deal with it differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You've spoken with Mr. Delalic many times in the last year, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Is this a question to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I wasn't really on good terms with Ramiz Delalic since 1996. As for Ramiz Delalic, Celo, I can only say that this is a man who saved those children. I'm nobody's agent here. I'm just a witness of this Tribunal to confirm what actually happened. As for your putting to me that I'm someone's agent --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Come back -- come back to the question, please. You've met with him many times in the last 12 months.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Have you met with him ever in the past 12 months?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: In the past 12 months -- or rather, some 5 -- it's been now 5 months that this gentleman is in jail now. And for the remainder of the period, the person was abroad, out of reach of the Bosnian-Herzegovinian authorities. So I never talked to him. I never saw him. And I never crossed the borders of Bosnia-Herzegovina or Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you speak to him on the telephone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In the last 12 months, you haven't spoken with Ramiz Delalic at all? Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Only once, when Azem Mehonjic, the lawyer, was there, who told me that Ramiz was saying that I should tell the truth and not that Sefer Halilovic had not been commander of the Operation Neretva. That's when the lawyer phoned Ramiz and then Ramiz told me over the phone, "You should only tell the truth." That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what did Ramiz have to do with it? Why did you need to speak to Ramiz about that topic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: How should I know? Perhaps he was afraid that I was going to be influenced or intimidated by someone. But again, I repeat, the man only told me to tell the truth and nothing but.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Witness D, we are now going to go back to the beginning of your involvement in these matters. In -- in August of 1993, you were a member of the 9th Brigade and the assault company of that brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in whose platoon were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: The commander of my platoon of the assault detachment was Malco Rovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And under Rovcanin, however, there were three platoon commanders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what were their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: There was nay Nevzet Sabanovic, Samir Pilica, and I don't know the name of the third one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, Ramiz Delalic was a commander who was very strict about the use of alcohol and drugs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And he would not tolerate such behaviour from his troops; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: He punished his men if they took drugs. He tied them to radiators. He wouldn't let them go out. He did everything he could to get them off drugs, even imprisoned them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What he did not do was to report them to the police; is that the fact? He dealt with them himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will object again to this question on the basis he's asking a question of the witness as to what another person did or did not do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So what's the problem for that? I see no problem for that. The witness could answer yes or no, you know. I don't see any problem. You may proceed, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Witness D, that's the fact, isn't it? Ramiz Delalic dealt with those problems internally and did not involve the police, either military police or civilian police; is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I tell you he gave them over to the military police in the central prison, the military prison. He sent them to prison for that. He didn't deal with this on his own. He was not a judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No. I --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: It was other authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Which authorities was it who tied people to the -- to the radiator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Well, authorities. Those who came. People were undergoing some sort of crisis. I don't know what kind of a feeling that is, but you had to guard them until the police came. You had to calm them down. I didn't really mean to keep them tied to radiators like dogs or animals, as you seem to interpret it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm not interpreting anything, Witness D. I'm just asking you what the facts are. But to proceed. To your -- from what you noticed and what you saw, Ramiz Delalic commanded a great deal of loyalty from his troops; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: We were like, well, ordinary privates. But he also behaved like a simple soldier. He didn't act like a commander. We had our brigade commander who was also just like an ordinary soldier. Ramiz Delalic, Celo, never really acted as if he was different from other men. We were all soldiers together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But if Ramiz gave an order, so far as you could observe in that -- in your part of the 9th Brigade, it was obeyed; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: He received these orders from someone, and then he gave them to us and we had to do whatever it was, follow orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But just deal with the question you're being asked, please. When Ramiz Delalic gave an order, from what you observed, it was obeyed in the 9th Brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: He only gave us combat orders. Nothing else. The ones he received from the Supreme Command. He received all sorts of orders from the gentlemen in the Supreme Command and then he told us what the orders were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, in July of 1993, there was an incident involving a confrontation between some of your soldiers from the 9th Brigade and some members of the civilian police; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I know about it, but I didn't participate in it. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In relation to that incident, what you know -- what you know from being there at the time, from being in Sarajevo at the time, was that members of the military -- sorry, members of the civilian police were disarmed by some 9th Brigade members for a short period of time and then they were released. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were released. But I don't know why this happened or how it actually happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay, Witness D. I'm not going to press you about the reasons. But following upon that confrontation, the -- a man named Fikret Muslimovic was dismissed from his post in military security and the head of the 1st Corps was also replaced - that was Talijan - who was in charge of the 1st Corps. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, Ramiz Delalic was not present during the killings in Grabovica, was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And one thing you can say for sure is that when Ramiz Delalic was present, the soldiers used to behave themselves very well, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: He arrived in Grabovica only when he brought those children there, and all the soldiers were afraid, the ones who were lined up, because I am certain he would have killed the man who committed the crime had they been in the line-up. I assert that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. That's okay. Don't -- just deal with the question you're being asked and it will go a little bit quicker, Witness D. The truth is that when Delalic was present, not just in Grabovica but at other places too, the soldiers would behave themselves well. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, what you say about Mr. Delalic also is that he made what appeared to you to be a bona fide genuine effort to find out who the killers were; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, he asked the children to identify the killers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And as far as you could see, at that point Mr. Delalic was not covering up this crime but was trying to uncover it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Why didn't you tell him who the criminals were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Because those men were not there and they all went to Jablanica after that and Celo went back with the children and Mr. Sefer Halilovic and Zuka and Vehbija Karic, where they all met. I'm sure they discussed what happened. But then they covered it up. The Supreme Command was all there. The Chief of Staff, your client, Mr. Sefer Halilovic, was there. Why didn't he take any action? Why didn't he bring that unit back and act as he should have to have the crime uncovered? You're asking me to say something that didn't happen. He should have done that. Ramiz Delalic wasn't able to. I wasn't able to. They could have shot the whole unit and that would have been the end of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But just come back to my question though. You knew who the real killers were, so why didn't you go to Ramiz Delalic and tell him that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember why.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Is it because you were one of the killers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No, I wasn't a killer. I told you, had I been a killer, I would confess it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. When you departed on the 7th of September from the base at Trampina Street, Sefer Halilovic was not there; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No. Mr. Karavelic was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You were addressed by Mr. Karavelic and he told you what the operation was about; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, Operation Neretva and that the Supreme Commander of that operation was Mr. Sefer Halilovic, as he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did he tell you whether Sefer Halilovic was the Chief of Staff or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I knew he was the Chief of Staff. He was not the commander of the army, however. Throughout the war, he was the Chief of Staff. From the first day when he joined the army, he was the Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And was it your understanding that he was in the same position now that he was in at the start of the war, Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I think so, yes. Maybe his position is stronger. Time has elapsed and the army was no longer groups of 10 or 20 soldiers in the streets but brigades were established and it was under his command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. You knew very well he'd been replaced as commander of the army by Rasim Delic early in June of 1993. You knew that, didn't you, Witness D?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No, that's not correct that Rasim Delic replaced him. Rasim Delic was appointed to an establishment post that had not been filled, commander of the army. Sefer Halilovic was the Chief of Staff of the army. You're talking about something else. Sefer Halilovic was never the commander of the army establishment-wise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And according to you, is the position this: You were told that your unit would be subordinated -- sorry, that your -- you would be commanded by Zuka? Is that what you say you were told at -- at the barracks at Trampina Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, that's a different area of responsibility, another corps. That's something else altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You mentioned the name of Gusic earlier on. Were you told that the immediate commander to Zuka was going to be Salko Gusic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Salko Gusic was there. It was -- the 4th and the 6th Corps. And whether they had been joined together at that point, I don't know. Salko Gusic was the commander of the 6th Corps. There was also the 4th Corps. I can't remember at what time those two corps were joined and had a single commander. Salko Gusic was there --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the question is: Were you told at Trampina Street that Zuka's unit was under Gusic or not

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Were you told whether or not Gusic had any involvement while you were there at Trampina Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: They didn't mention any other commanders except for Sefer Halilovic, who was mentioned by Mr. Karavelic. He said, "Our Chief of Staff, the commander of Operation Neretva will be Mr. Sefer Halilovic and he will issue all the orders, as he issued an order to withdraw after two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Are you -- let me ask you a question: Are you -- I withdraw it. I'll proceed another way. Your account is that Ramiz was not the commander of the units that came down in the truck; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No. We were under the command of Zulfikar Alispago, known as Zuka. Ramiz Delalic, Celo, had no connection with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But he was there in the truck with you on the way down to Jablanica, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Are you protecting Ramiz Delalic in your evidence here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Are you sure he had no function and no connection with you troops at all on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No, he had no orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did he --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: And when we --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, did he arrive in Jablanica with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In fact, for a short period of time, did he come on actually and join you in the village of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: He came with the children. That was on the 9th, at about 3.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Is that the only occasion you ever saw him in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, the only occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did he ever take up a position in the white house that you accommodated yourself in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Only afterwards, when we went into action. I don't know whether he spent that night there between the 9th and the 10th, when we went into action.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, when you arrived in Jablanica, it was the fact that Zuka came and met - and Zuka -- by "Zuka" I mean Zulfikar Alispago - Zuka meant and spoke to your group. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. He found accommodation for us. It was in front of his base, in Donja Jablanica. He said he would find accommodation for us that, he would take care of food for us, and everything else that we needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But it's a bit more than that. He told you that accommodation was already arranged in Grabovica, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure he agreed about accommodation. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And after that, you were taken and escorted by three or four of Zuka's soldiers to Grabovica; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. He gave us blankets and some sort of mattresses to sleep on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And how many of you did he give blankets and some sort of mattresses to sleep on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Well, whoever lacked these things. They came to the truck and this was distributed. Whoever needed these things was issued with them, if they couldn't find mattresses or blankets in the house where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You were then escorted to Grabovica by a soldier of Zuka's with the nickname of Spaga; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't mention that. I don't know. Spaga? It sounds familiar. Yes, I know the man, but I don't know whether he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just to be clear about the dates: You left Sarajevo on the 7th and you arrived in Jablanica on the morning of the 8th. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You then took up residence in an empty house, white in colour; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you take up residence there with Dino Arnautovic, the logistics man from your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, but we didn't go in because it was dirty and neglected. The house had to be cleaned out. So we were in front of the house, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was Malco Rovcanin also detailed to go and stay in that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was Ramiz Delalic, at that early stage, detailed to go into that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was supposed to be put up there, but when he arrived with those children, he was in front of that house. He was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: But he didn't sleep there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No. But just in terms of the children, that's later. I'm talking about when you arrived there. Is your position this: That Ramiz Delalic --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: -- or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No. No, he wasn't with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you've never told anyone that he was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No, I didn't tell anyone that he was or that he slept there that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, this house smelled very bad, didn't it, Witness, Witness D?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it was dirty.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And not just dirty. It smelt bad too; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And it had no electricity; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And it didn't have any running order either; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in short, it looks like you got the worse house in the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: It was the only one left over.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, other soldiers had houses where there was heating, water, electricity, and food; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: We didn't look for it. We got food from Zuka. There was electricity in all the houses. We didn't need heating because it was summertime. And we brought electricity in from the neighbouring house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: In fact, it was wartime and we had lived in Sarajevo for a long time without electricity or water or food, and we could sleep under the open sky, out in the open.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But just to jump ahead a little bit. You indicated that there was a soldier who complained about their -- their accommodation conditions. Now --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was it you who had the worst accommodation conditions of everyone in the village? You, Witness D?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No, I didn't have the worst accommodation. I was satisfied with the accommodation. I cleaned the house. I knew we wouldn't stay there long. And the weather was nice and I could sleep out in the open.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What's the use of cleaning the house if you could sleep out in the open?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Well, for purposes of my personal hygiene.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. All right. And on that first day and evening that you spent in -- in Grabovica, you've indicated to the Prosecutor that you visited some other people and that ultimately you went quietly to bed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And so through that -- that evening -- that afternoon and evening of the 8th, you heard no screaming by terrified Croat civilians; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You saw no 9th Brigade members or any other people shooting innocent civilians; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Not that night, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You saw no one trying to flee the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: That night, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You heard no drunken soldiers singing and celebrating; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: There was no drinking that night. There were no drunken soldiers. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Did you observe any alcohol in the village on that night, the 8th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what about Mr. Mehanovic? Where was he that night, the night of the 8th? Was he in the village with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, he was in the village with us. He slept in a house higher up than the one where Musa was. I don't know. Maybe -- I can show it to you if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm going to show you those pictures in just a moment. What about Mr. Arnautovic? Did he stay with you that first night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, he was with us and he slept outside in the open.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And did he have a vehicle with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: He didn't have a jeep, a brown jeep with a white roof?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: He didn't drive backwards and forwards to Jablanica to collect supplies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Well, we received food every day from Zuka's headquarters, breakfast, lunch, and dinner. No other supplies were needed. And Zuka's soldiers brought that food in. As far as I know, Dino didn't bring anything in except that he distributed cigarettes, rations of cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, he's given evidence in this court and I'm going to have to ask you to comment on this. He's given sworn evidence here that he went backwards and forwards to Jablanica on a number of occasions on the 8th. But you're claiming -- you can say he was there with you in the village without a car; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know. Believe me, I can neither confirm nor deny this. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, why can't you deny it, given the evidence you gave two minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: He was there with me, and whether he went or didn't go, I don't know. I can't say whether he went or not. I can't remember the details after so much time, whether he went to get food or not, whether the food was late or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Let me ask you this question: Are you prepared to adapt your evidence whenever it looks like one of your friends is in trouble? Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Look, I want to put something to you in general terms, Witness D. I want to put to you that what really happened on the afternoon of the 8th is that some of you soldiers commenced killing and ill-treating Croat civilians in Grabovica starting at around approximately 6.00 p.m. and that the killing, the ill-treatment, the drunkenness, and the terrorising just went on from there. Do you agree or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Let me be quite clear about something. You have always said that the first day and night passed peacefully, haven't you? That's always been your position. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, from the 8th to the 9th, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Do you happen to know -- is it within your knowledge that Mr. Mehanovic says the same thing, that the first day and night passed by in peace; namely, the night of the 8th and over into the 9th? Do you know that that's what Mehanovic says too?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I mean, I object on the grounds that he's using the testimony of another witness. It's the way it's being done, Your Honour, in the sense that does he know that Mr. Mehanovic is saying this or the other. I mean, I agree that now it is evidence in court and he may refer to it, but it's got to be in an appropriate manner and not tell the witness what Mr. Mehanovic is saying or not saying and does he know whether Mr. Mehanovic said certain things. Perhaps the question could be framed in -- in more concrete terms, Your Honour, and -- and referenced to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, there's no problem for the -- for the Defence team to use the testimony of the previous witness to challenge or put a question to this witness, but maybe this question is not in the proper form and maybe Mr. Morrissey could put it in another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I hope it is in the proper form. When Your Honour raises the possibility of a problem, I'll put it differently. But I don't want my learned friend to make objections like that. That wasn't a proper objection. As Your Honour will see, it started with one thing, it ended with another. It's not a proper way to object. However, if there be any lack of clarity, that doesn't help the Defence and I won't persist with the question, if it's raising that sort of issue. Well -- no, Your Honour, I would seek to persist with that transcript. Your Honour, could I just justify it by regard to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour understands and the Court understands that I'm putting collusion. I'm putting that there's been an agreement. Now, that question goes directly to that issue and really is the only way you can ask that. But I think there is another way, which I'll -- which I'll deal with, Your Honour. I've thought of it so I'll deal with it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Witness D, you agreed upon your story as to that first night passing by peacefully with your friends Mehanovic and Arnautovic, didn't you? You agreed on that many years ago; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Do you have any explanation for why it is that Mr. Mehanovic says the same thing you say, that the first night passed in peace and quiet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I have no explanation for that. I really have no idea why Mr. Mehanovic made such a statement. I wasn't there nor did I read Mr. Mehanovic's statements nor did I enquire of him as to what sort of a statement he gave --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: -- wherever it was. Nor am I interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. I can understand that. Do you know why -- or do you have any explanation for why it is that Mr. Arnautovic says the same thing you say, that the night of the 8th and into the 9th passed in peace?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know. The same goes for Mr. Arnautovic, just as I stated in -- in relation to an earlier question. I have no idea why this is so. There was no agreement, nor am -- nor is it my business what they stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And beyond what you've just said, you have no other explanation to offer for why it is that you three friends are telling the same totally wrong story; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I know that this is a truthful account. Now, you can claim otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, your claim is that the meeting where Karic made the comment about Croats occurred at about lunchtime the following day; is that correct? Is that your claim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, in the presence of Mr. Sefer, Zuka, Vehbija Karic, Salko Gusic, and some other commanders that I don't know, Sadic, and others. Yes, that's what I claim and that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, what I want to put to you is something quite different: I put to you that a group of staff officers came along on the afternoon of the 8th, the very afternoon that you arrived. And I want to put to you that those staff officers were Vehbija Karic, Zicro Suljevic, Rifat Bilajac, Namik Dzankovic, and Huso Alic from Zuka's Unit. I put it to you that they arrived not on the 9th and not after a night of peace but a short time, within hours, after you arrived at -- at Grabovica. Do you agree or disagree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I disagree. They arrived on the 9th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I put it to you that they held no mass meeting or line-up of the kind that you've described at all. Do you agree or disagree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: This was no line-up. People were sitting. Sefer addressed the group, but it wasn't like a line-up in the strictest sense. They were all sitting around. There was a lawn there. And they were being told what they were supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Do you use the term "line-up" earlier on in your evidence in chief or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Well, did Mr. Karic have with him his son?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Mr. Karic? No. I don't know his son either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No. Well, do you know whether his son's half Croatian or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: See, to your knowledge, Vehbija Karic was a very experienced staff officer, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: An artillery man.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And he was very senior in the Bosnian army; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Certainly so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And he had the nickname of Amidza, uncle, A-m-i-d-z-a; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know about his nickname. I've never heard such a nickname of his, nor did anybody inform me about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, at page 19 of the transcript in the evidence that you gave today, did you say this, page 19 at line 3 - and I'll start in fairness to you at line 2 - "At that point, Vehbija Karic, Sefer Halilovic, Zuka, and other commanders from the SUP Supreme Command who were there came. They lined up all the units that were there and the units were lined up just in front of the house where -- where I slept in, because there was a plain, a plateau there where everybody could be lined up"? Now, was that your evidence maybe an hour ago or so in this Tribunal, where you said "lined up" three times in one paragraph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: First of all, Sefer Halilovic and Vehbija Karic did not line up the soldiers. It was the commanders of the platoons -- or rather, of the units who called on the soldiers to show up. They said this unit should be here, this unit should be there. After that, all of them were seated there. So it wasn't Sefer or Vehbija who lined them up. They all gathered, sat down, and that's when they were told about Operation Neretva. So there were units of the 9th Motorised Brigade, Cedo's Wolves, Zuka's men, the Independent Battalion. All of these units numbering some 100 to 150 troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Well, Witness D, is your position this: That that line-up or sitdown or whatever it was took place at 12.00, or did it take place at 3.00 in the afternoon? What's your account about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know whether these three hours make any difference, really. I didn't have a watch to be able to pay any attention to the time. I know that it was around noontime. Whether it was noon, 12.00, whether it was 1.00, 2.00, or 3.00 in the afternoon, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, is the reason you don't know because the whole meeting is just made up by you and you can tell the big picture but you can't remember the details? Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I didn't make up anything. I told you what had happened, and I'm sure that they -- "they" meaning those commanders who were there -- that they knew the course of events but simply refused to say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What's the name of the six companions who were sitting with you when these commanders arrived in the jeeps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know. I, Dino, Nevzet Sabanovic, Sulejman Lujinovic. I don't know. I can't remember their names. This was long ago, 1993, then 1998. I can't recall all the names, but I'm sure the people who were there, they know these men, just as I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. So to the best of your -- what you're saying here is that you, Sabanovic -- sorry, yourself, Sabanovic, Dino Arnautovic,-- and I'm sorry, I've just forgotten. You did mention another person, Sule Lujinovic - is that correct - were sitting there when these people arrived in their jeeps. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: We were making lunch, and at that point I was extracting honey from a honeycomb there, and that's when I offered the honey to the commanders who had just arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. But even on these matters of detail, Mr. Witness, I have to ask you: Didn't you tell the Tribunal earlier on that Dino Arnautovic was one of the drivers of these jeeps? This was at page 12 -- just hold on a second. I'll put the transcript so there's no unfairness to you. At page 22 --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... hang on a second, then. This is what we want to put. This is at line 6 of page 22: "The other jeep was driven by Dino." And then the Prosecutor asked another question. Mr. Morrissey made an objection. And the objection was: "I wonder if my friend would like to clarify the identity of this person who's called Dino here because we have a Dino who gave evidence." His Honour Judge Liu said: "Yes." And you then said "Dino Arnautovic" also known as "Dino." Do you remember giving that evidence? That's not a difficult question there. Could you please --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No, no. That was Dino Arnautovic. I mentioned him as my fellow colleague from my brigade. He was there. He came with them and was there with us. That was before all the military men arrived later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I see. So your position is that Dino was there with you before the military men arrived. He then left and brought them back in a jeep. Is that what you're claim is, your claim now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No. He had come with the gentlemen, and that's why I counted him in. I factored him in as being there before all the troops gathered up. So he wasn't seated with the commanders. He was there with us. He had brought them over and was then there with us as one of the men in -- in my company, until all the troops gathered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. And, of course, it -- the other two people who you say were there, were they people from the same house as Mr. Lujinovic ...?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know precisely which house they were from. I just know that Nevzet Sabanovic was in the same house that I slept in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, did you say to my learned friend Ms. Chana in proofing that this meeting took place at 1500 hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: It is possible. I don't know the exact hour. I told you that it was around noon. I did not specify the time because I didn't know the exact time of their arrival.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, just let me be clear about this. Did you say -- did you specify the time to my learned friend here, Ms. Chana, "At 1500 hours the commanders came to Grabovica"? Did you specify 1500 hours to Ms. Chana who's sitting here in court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: It is possible that I said that it was at 3.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, it's not just a question of it being possible. That's what you told her, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Well, fine. Yes, I did say so, but I don't know the exact hour. It's been 12 years. I suppose you can understand. I can't recall what happened yesterday, let alone 10 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Why can't you recall what happened yesterday? Have you got a bad memory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: It's not that I have a bad memory. You're just asking for very specific pieces of information and you're on a lookout for a reason to ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, I'll just come to some other specifics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe it's time for a break before we come to other specifics.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just considering whether there's -- yes. Yes. Yes, Your Honour, it should be about time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a break and we'll resume at quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey. Please lead us to the specifics.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness D. Witness D, before the break, I was asking you questions about the meeting that you've described where Mr. Karic made his blood-thirsty comment, and I wanted to ask you this: Of the people who were there, you indicated that the platoon commanders had effectively fetched or procured the soldiers. So I take it from that that Nihad Vlahovljak was present at this gathering. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you're familiar too with some other individuals connected with Vlahovljak, with the nicknames Dzigi, Klos, and Hajre. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And they were there at this gathering according to you as well; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So you would say that at the time this gathering of yours took place that they weren't sitting around a table at Pero Maric's house with Enes Sakrak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: The meeting with Vehbija Karic, Sefer Halilovic and others? Is that what you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Clearly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: At that point, all the soldiers were on the paddock outside this house where Mr. Sefer, Vehbija Karic, and others were seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And because according to you, this is a very important meeting with the Chief of Staff of the whole Bosnian army present; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Sefer Halilovic was there. He was talking about Operation Neretva and about how we would not return at any cost until the siege of Mostar had been lifted and things to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Look, what I want to put to you is that the account given by Mr. Sakrak is truly the correct one, and that is that he and his companions, including Vlahovljak, spent that afternoon at the Pero Maric house with Pero Maric and without any meetings such as the one you're now alleging. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: That took place on the 8th and not on the 9th, sir. We are talking about a meeting that took place on the 9th and not on the 8th. Because the night on the 8th was a peaceful one when nothing took place. I am talking about the meeting that took place in the afternoon hours of the 9th, where the officers and commanders were present.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I understand that's your evidence. And -- very well. Well, I want to come now to the -- the questions about the -- the killing of Pero Maric. How long before he was killed did you find yourself at the Pero Maric house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I wasn't in the house at all. I was in front of the house, where there was a table.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. The question is: How long before the killing did you arrive there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Perhaps an hour. I was having a coffee with Nihad and others who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And who else was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: His soldiers who were members of his unit. We weren't really close. I only know Nihad Vlahovljak and others I only knew by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And that included Klos; correct? K-l-o-s?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know. Believe me, I don't know their names. If I saw them, perhaps I'd be able to tell you that such-and-such were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. You had been a member of the 9th Brigade assault company since it was founded; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In fact, along with your friend Nedzad Mehanovic, you had joined the precursor brigade to the 9th Brigade on the 22nd of July the previous year, on the same day as Mr. Mehanovic. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. We were reassigned from the 1st Sandzak Unit into the military police unit at the time, because it wasn't a brigade yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay. And so you knew all of the people in that unit by name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And those people included Dzigi, Hajre, Pedja, and Klos; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I apologise. You seem to be talking about a different unit altogether. This unit was under a different command. There was the 3rd Mountain Brigade that joined with another and then formed the 9th Motorised Brigade. We were at the time military police under the command of Nedzarovic [phoen]. So this was one platoon, a company of some 30 men that was based at a school, and there was no brigade there, not was there any Dzigi --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... all right just stope there for a moment. I'll just deal with the matter differently --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: And there wasn't a school there. Nor was there a Dzigi --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. The 9th Brigade assault platoon had been in existence for several months at the time of September 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I haven't understood your question. Several months before what?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The assault platoon had been in existence for several months before the killings that you witnessed; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you knew by name the members of that assault company; is that correct? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you knew the individuals that I just listed, Dzigi -- well, I'll take them -- I withdraw that question. You knew Dzigi, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: This gentleman wasn't a member of my assault detachment. He was in a unit in a completely different battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and was he sitting around the table when Pero Maric was shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I didn't know the gentleman and I don't know whether he was seated next to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You knew an individual with the name Hajre; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I met Hajre on that same day, and I do remember him to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and he was sitting at the table too, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Hajre was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... an individual called Pedja. Q.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, do you know an individual named Galic, Serbian background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You knew Nihad, and he was sitting at the table; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Nihad Vlahovljak?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. He was sitting at the table; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And you knew a man called --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: He was there with me having a coffee.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you knew a man called Prasovic, also with the nickname of Klos, and he was at the table; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And those people were all at the table before you got there; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't make a statement to this effect. I didn't know that. I didn't know the people at all. These were -- there were two brigades that merged into one. And these people were not members of my assault detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay. Now, you say that an individual walked in and shot -- walked in and within 20 seconds he shot Pero Maric dead; is that correct? Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. I entered the house. We were --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was Pero Maric seated at the table when he was shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you arrive with this individual who did the shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you say you arrived alone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. He didn't arrive with you, did he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: He didn't come with me. I came before him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You didn't take a packet of cigarettes out of the dead man's pocket, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No. I had enough cigarettes of my own. I didn't need to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Well, did you see that done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Where do you say Pero Maric was when the bullet hit him? Sitting at the table or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: He was in his house. That's what I said ten times already. I don't want to repeat myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's all right. Standing or sitting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know. I did not see that. I only know that he was in his house. I didn't even know his name until I talked to the people at the UN premises in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, after you saw that -- well, perhaps I should ask you this. Did you see that shooting or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So is your position that you were seated at the coffee table but you didn't see the shooting? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: How could I have seen it when it took place in the house? Otherwise, I would have said that I had seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. So did you watch the shooter walk into the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. He entered the house. I don't know if -- I didn't know what was going to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Are you sure that that's the truth? You didn't know what was going to happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I'm certain of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What did you see happen when the shooter walked into the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Nothing. I only heard a shot, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did he close the door behind him when he entered the house or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, you were there. What did you see? Did he close the door or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What did you see when you were looking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I wasn't looking at all. I was seated at the table unsuspecting of a murder to take place. You're asking me questions that I simply ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Did you see the body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you ever see the body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Pero Maric's? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Is Pero Maric's body one of those taken away in the trucks by Zuka's soldiers, Mr. Witness D?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: You should ask Zuka about this. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you. You accuse Zuka of taking bodies away in trucks, and I'm asking you: Was the victim of the murder that you were nearby to taken away in one of those trucks or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't collecting dead bodies. It was Zuka's men who did that. I never saw the dead bodies in Grabovica because I myself did not collect them nor was I aware at the time of someone collecting them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Let me ask you another question about that. Are you sure you weren't one of the chief diggers and buriers of bodies in this criminal sequence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No, I never dug any graves nor buried the people there. I didn't know about people being buried in Grabovica. I only know what I said, that -- I know that they were killed. But where they were buried, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. So how did you know that somebody had been shot inside the house at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Because the gentleman got out and Vlahovljak told him, "What are you doing?" And the other one retorted in some manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what were the words he used when he retorted in some manner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Nihad asked him, "What are you doing? Are you out of your mind?" And the other one said, "Under beware that the same fate doesn't befall you as had befallen the other man." He turned round and left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you go inside and have a look to see what had happened to the other man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I didn't go inside, but the others did. Nihad went in, and then came out to tell us that the man was dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What about the woman? Did he tell you that as well or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, he said that there was a man and that there was a woman. Both were killed. That the madman had killed both the man and the woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So the woman, having been killed at that point, it wouldn't be possible for anyone to hear her crying in the night after the shooting of Pero Maric in her bedroom; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I wasn't there, because at that point I returned to the house that I was accommodated in and we were commenting upon the madness that reigned and about how this was all brought on by what Vehbija Karic had said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, how long did you remain at the Maric house before you left back for your own house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I never entered the house, I told you. I stayed there for some ten minutes and then went back to the house that I slept in. It wasn't my house; it was the house they slept in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in that ten minutes, did you ask any details of those who had been inside and claimed to have seen the bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No. They just came out and said that a man and a woman had been killed and that was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did anyone have any cigarettes from the body of the man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I didn't go in, I told you. I have no idea whether someone had taken cigarettes or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did people appear to -- well, I withdraw that. And did you speak to Nihad and say, "What are we going to do about this?"

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you speak to any of the others and say, "What are we going to do about this?"

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Nobody said anything about it nor acted upon it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Why didn't you say to the others, "What a disgusting horrifying thing. What are we going to do"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: All the soldiers who were there were aware of this and did nothing. I don't know. I have no answer to give.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Why didn't you suggest, "Let's go and talk to Ramiz. There's been a murder of civilians committed"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Well, Nihad Vlahovljak, as a commander there, should have done that, assumed responsibility, because it was the house that he slept in and he should have done something about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Who was your commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Nevzet Sabanovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Did you tell him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No, at that point he was conducting reconnaissance at the beater, at the antenna, at the hillock in the locality of Vrdi, Vrdi. Whatever it was called.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Could you just tell us how we spell his name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Nevzet Sabanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. And Antena hill at Vrdi that, -- is that the area where you were in combat later on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Well -- and Mr. Sabanovic was conducting that reconnaissance because of the need to -- to effectively reconnoiter the scene of the battle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: He received such an order from Sefer Halilovic that reconnaissance troops be sent over there to get acquainted with the terrain because we had never had any actions in Herzegovina prior to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. You see, he's one of the people that you said was there when the honey was being offered to Vehbija Karic, isn't he? Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, yes, upon their arrival.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. So what you want to say is that he'd been sent off for reconnaissance after that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: After the meeting on the 9th, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. And you can be quite clear about that, can't you, that he was sent away on the afternoon of the 9th, Mr. Sabanovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. He set off in the afternoon and he waited for us in the village of Dreznica, which was where we set out for our action from.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, who was in command in his absence of your platoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Nobody.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Why didn't you tell Malco Rovcanin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know. I believe that Malco wasn't around at the time of the first murder at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Look, this wasn't the sort of thing that happened every day, was it, that an innocent civilian would just be shot dead in his own home by one of your brigade members. So I'm going to repeat the question to you: Why didn't you do something, tell someone, take some action? And if not that, why didn't you discuss doing that with someone of the people sitting around at the table?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I didn't do anything about it because it was not within my power. The one who should have done so is the person you're representing, so you should ask him why he never did anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... why -- sorry. Why didn't you go and ask Sefer Halilovic? Why didn't you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Because he never showed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Why didn't you go in to Jablanica and tell him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: What with? On a bicycle? Take a walk?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Isn't the truth of the matter -- well, just a moment. You know that some refugees were put in the position of having to take that walk, don't you? You know that; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: The Muslim refugees were on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sure. You know that some Croat refugees fleeing from the killings made that very walk to Jablanica in their 70s; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Isn't the fact really this, that from the moment that Pero Maric was killed you have been covering up your own role from that day until this minute? Is that the fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No, I had no one to report it to. Everyone was covering it up, from Sefer Halilovic on. Why should I be to blame?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And when Ramiz -- why did you mention Sefer Halilovic at that point then particularly, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Because he was the one in charge, responsible for the entire operation, for the entire region in Herzegovina. At that point in time, the man was Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The question is: Why did you mention his name in evidence at this moment? Perhaps I can suggest to you -- I'll put a proposition to you: Whenever you're put under pressure in these questions, what you're going to do is to say "Sefer Halilovic was the commander," "Sefer Halilovic should have done something," and "Sefer Halilovic is the person who's covered it up."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... because you're the killer; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I'm not a killer and you're accusing me without evidence. If you show me evidence, then I'd accept it. But if I had been a killer, I would have confessed so. The man responsible for the killings is the one seated next to you there, your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In fairness to you, I'll put -- point the evidence to you that I'm going to point out so that you know where this is going. You in your constant, what we put to you as dishonest has denials of your involvement, minimised your role, and concealed your presence at Pero Maric's death and at other criminal acts precisely because you were the author of those acts. You understand that proposition that's being put to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I wasn't the author of these acts, nor do I know why these things happened. All the people who were there were responsible for the crimes because they were covering up the same acts, from ordinary privates up to the most senior officers. Let's say frankly that it wasn't in the interest of the Supreme Command to clarify the whole event, and it could have been all cleared up after Operation Neretva had taken place. Now, why they chose not to, this is something I don't know. You should ask the gentlemen from the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Now, that I was supposed to come and report to Sefer Halilovic that this is the way things happened ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Morrissey, I believe that this lines of the questioning become a little bit more argumentative.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You're doubtless correct, Your Honour. And there's a new line occurring.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Witness D, in 1995 you became aware that Sefer Halilovic in a newspaper article published in Oslobodjenje and subsequently republished in other publications demanded in public that the Grabovica crime be investigated; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No. I heard a different account. Sefer Halilovic received an order from the commander of the army, Rasim Delic - that's what I heard from the media in Sarajevo - that he should assume responsibility for an investigation into the events in Grabovica. When he received the paper containing the order, he tore it apart. You can ask the gentleman why he did so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just speak to the question I'm asking you. In 1995 --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just a moment. In 1995, you became aware that Halilovic called for an investigation; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you dispute that in an article published in Oslobodjenje in 1995 that Sefer Halilovic did call for an investigation. Do you dispute that or do you accept it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You don't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It wasn't a matter of concern to you and other members of the 9th Brigade that Sefer Halilovic was demanding a public inquiry into the Grabovica matter? That didn't concern you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: It didn't concern me because I wasn't guilty of anything. I hadn't done anything wrong. My soul is pure, and I can look at it with open eyes. As for the perpetrators and as for what was done, there was some sort of conflict between Mr. Halilovic and Rasim Delic. One was a commander; the other one was not. Sefer Halilovic created the army and then Rasim Delic arrived when he had already done all the hard work, and so there was this conflict between them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The man who shot Pero Maric was Musa Hota, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You were prepared to name Musa Hota as a potential rapist in your initial statement to the police in 1993 on the 31st of October; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I believe we went into closed session when I asked some of these questions because of the witness's expression that he may be compromised by giving some of these names, and I believe this is one of the names that came up. Perhaps we can do this in -- in closed session when it comes to the names. It's the same reason we went into closed session the last time, Your Honour. We were talking about perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you know, I mean, for this Tribunal we're only concerned about the -- the status of the witness. If this person is going to testify in this Tribunal, his identity should be protected. But if you say this matter is related to some privacy of a person, that might be a reason. Well, Mr. Morrissey, do you mind that we go into the private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I do object to it, Your Honour. I object to it. The -- frankly, the identity of the murderer is not in doubt. It's in evidence already that that man's pleaded guilty and is serving a sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no, no. I don't mean the murderer. I mean that -- you know, the incident concerning of naming somebody as a rapist.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: If that's a matter that arises, he's not here, he's not represented, it could be an unfairness to him. I accept that -- that that -- that for the -- for the purpose of me asking that question, we could go into private session. But the answer doesn't have to be in private session. But the allegation can be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- well, we'll see, you know. Let's go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... and when you woke up the next morning, you were aware -- When you woke up the next morning, you were aware that Musa Hota was the killer of the -- of Pero Maric; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No. No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You don't know? You don't know who that killer was? Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: How can I tell you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, you were there and you saw him come and walk into the house with the rifle, according to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: A soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You're saying you can't --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: A soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But you know what Musa Hota looks like, don't you? You know him; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I didn't mention Musa Hota at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. You knew Musa Hota. You knew what he looked like, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I know Musa Hota.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. So what you're saying is the person who walked in and shot Pero Maric was not Musa Hota; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I have no answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
