utterances.text: The reason you don't have an answer to it is because your whole story is one packet of lies from the beginning of the end, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No. It's for my own safety. As to who has confessed and who is in prison for that, that's a different story. As to who killed Pero Maric, when you asked me to tell you the names, I did -- something else was being asked of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit P4, the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Witness, you're about to be shown an exhibit here. It's a photograph. And what I'm going to ask is that you be given the chance to mark this photograph. And I want you to mark on this photograph where were the bodies you saw on the day following the shooting of Pero Maric.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be assisted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just do them with numbers. Don't worry about putting crosses. Just put numbers near each body -- where each body you saw was located.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Along the road. There was one up here and then the rest were along the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you indicate to this Tribunal on your oath that you saw six bodies on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: This was on the 10th, the 10th, in the morning, when I got up around 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. This is -- according to you, it's the day following the killing of Pero Maric; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Pero Maric was killed in the afternoon, just as it was beginning to grow dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: On the 9th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I guess there's no objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The photograph will be Defence Exhibit D186.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would you just keep that in front of you now, please. Did you tell the Prosecution attorney in this case, Ms. Chana, that you saw - and I'll read to you from the proofing notes - did you tell Ms. Chana that "The next day, on the 10th of September, I saw many bodies, at least ten, in the village as I went for a walk about"? Did you tell her that just a couple of days ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: On that day, I saw five or six bodies. There may have been more bodies there. They must have brought them down there, because there was blood on the road and all along the road there were traces of blood and there were five or six corpses. Well, I didn't actually count them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know how many people were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, that's okay. But just persist with the question. Did you tell the attorney Ms. Chana what I just put to you, that you saw many bodies" -- just a moment. Wait. "I saw many body, at least 10 in the village, as I went for a walk about"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Five, six, ten. They were along the road. Only those along the road. I don't know where the other bodies were around the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just focus on the question you're being asked. Did you put that figure of 10 to Ms. Chana as her briefing notes provided to the Defence and the Tribunal indicate? Did you tell her that you saw "many bodies, at least 10, in the village"? Did you tell her that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I did. But I said "up to 10." Maybe five or six. I didn't really go along counting the bodies. I wasn't assigned the task of counting the victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So what you're saying about your comments to Ms. Chana are that you told her "five or six, up to ten"? Is that what your honest claim is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Quite honest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I call upon the Prosecutor to confirm what the situation is with this, because we have this document and I don't want to put the witness in a position of unfairness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is it necessary? I don't think so. Because, you know, the proofing notes is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: There's no problem of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As the Court pleases. Yes, as the Court pleases. Very well. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, as to the number of bodies that you saw, did you say in 1998 in a statement taken by Mr. Dragan Mijokovic dated the 20th of March, 1998, did you say this - and this is at the bottom of -- or the lower part of page 2, Your Honours, and Madam Prosecutor - did you say: "During the day, I saw the body of a male civilian, I think about 50 years old, below the road towards the Neretva. I know that there were several bodies next to the Neretva, although I did not see them myself"? Now, did you say that back in 1998 on the 20th of -- of March, that you saw one body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't remember. But as you just said, there were several other bodies, five or six bodies. As I'm saying now, I don't recall what I said seven years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Why did you tell Dragan Mijokovic in that statement that you only saw one? Why did you tell him that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: You just read out that I saw several other bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No. Let there be no doubt -- I don't want to do an -- I don't want to be unfair to you, Witness. I'll read it to you again so that you fully understand what's being put. Okay? "During the day, I saw the body of a male civilian, I think about 50 years old, below the road towards the Neretva. I know that there were several bodies next to the Neretva, although I did not see them myself." Now, why did you say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Although I didn't see them myself. There were other people who saw them, I didn't see them myself. I said that I -- no, what I said was I was not -- it was not me that saw them. There were other people there who saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, in another statement made to the cantonal court on the 30th of the 11th, 1998, did you say - and this is at page 4 of 5, Your Honours, at the top, and there's another passage towards the bottom that I'm going to go to as well, and Madam Prosecutor as well, it's about four of five lines from the top, I think -- perhaps six lines from the top - did you say this: "Together with Lujinovic, I got up and not far from the corner of the house on the road I saw a trace of blood. It looked as if a body was pulled over the dust and left a trace of blood. Lujinovic went towards his accommodation and I went towards the house where Nihad Vlahovljak was staying, because my friend Nedzad Mehanovic was also there. Walking there in the bushes next to the road I saw a man's body. I estimated that it was an old man, between 50 and 60 years old." Now, did you say that to the cantonal court and was that true, that you walked over to Vlahovljak's house and saw a body on the way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown the exhibit that was just tendered a minute ago, 186 -- P186. Thank you. It should be the marked exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you have that yet, Witness D, in front of you? Witness D, would you please indicate when you have it. Do you have it now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Okay. Now, looking at that photograph there, do you see the white house without a roof that you were billeted in, according to you? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And do you see partially hidden by the edge of the blue woodsmoke a small glimpse of Pero Maric's house among the bushes there? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, on the map that you've marked here in court, you've said nothing about a body on the path from your house over to Pero Maric's house, have you, on this drawing that you've marked already? You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't agree with you. All those statements we made were transcribed later on and they wrote down whatever suited them. What I'm saying here is the truth. And what we said back then, we were treated badly, we were locked up and beaten up by two strong men and then we had to say whatever they wanted and they constructed a story that suited them. That was in the MUP, the CSB, the -- whatever I said there, that's nothing. What I say here is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But is your position about the statement made to the cantonal court that you told the truth and they wrote it down wrongly, or is it that you were bashed by two strong men so that you told untruths? Which is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: First of all, they never let us read the statement. They would just say, "Sign here." Whatever statement I made in the MUP of the CSB, I was never allowed to read it, to look at it for five or ten minutes and really read it and then sign it as my statement. All this was set up. They wrote down whatever they wanted to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So was it set up if you mentioned that Sefer Halilovic was present as the commander of Neretva 93, or was that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: That was true. He was the commander. He knows it well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: -- of Operation Neretva.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I know. But if that information finds its way into one of these statements, is that set-up information that was bashed out of you by two strong men and then written down without your consent, or was that true information that you honestly gave and has been faithfully recorded? Which one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: First of all, all those statements that were made, it was never someone of Bosniak ethnicity who questioned you. They appointed Croats and Serbs to do that and they wrote down whatever they wanted. They weren't aiming at Sefer Halilovic and saying, "This is true. That is true." They were just adding this and that. Whoever did that, none of them was a Bosniak, of the people taking statements at that time. It was never a Bosniak questioning a member of the army or the 9th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So in that -- that hearing at the cantonal court, 30th of the 11th, 1998, investigating judge Ibrahim Hadzic, what ethnicity was he? That's on page 1 of the -- of that statement. What ethnicity was Judge Ibrahim -- investigating judge Ibrahim Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I never made a statement before that gentleman. It was Mr. Vladimir Spoljaric and Mijokovic that I made statements to. He's disabled. He lost an eye. But I never made a statement to that gentleman. Vladimir Spoljaric, 1993, the 26th of October to November, he was in charge of those proceedings and he was in charge of all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And since at the front of the record of the hearing of a witness on the 30th of the 11th, 1998, it's recorded "investigating judge, Ibrahim Hadzic, and clerk, Edina Djurdjevic." Do you maintain your position that you were only ever interviewed by Croats and Serbs, or would you like now to reconsider that claim.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No. No, I know I only made a statement to Mr. Vladimir Spoljaric and to Mijokovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. In your statement to Miodrag Mijokovic. You admit that you were sitting at that coffee table when Pero Maric was shot, did you? You never made any such admission to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Well, nobody was interested in clarifying the case. Nobody asked you those questions, "Did you see who killed someone?" Nobody asked who the murderers were. I'm telling you for the hundredth time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But didn't you advance the following completely false story - and I'm going to read it to you in complete and then I'll ask you some questions - and this is on page 1 and moving into page 2. This starts -- and your descriptions following what you say, following the visit by Mr. Karic and Sefer Halilovic. And what you've said is that after -- after recording what Karic said and what Halilovic said, you then went on to say this: "In the early evening of that day, Ramiz Delalic, Malco Rovcanin, and Fikret Kajevic left the village and went to do a job in Jablanica. Erdin Arnautovic, also known as Smrk [phoen], and I stayed in the house. At about 2300 or 2300 hours, the two of us went to bed and fell asleep. At about 0900 hours we got up." Now, would you agree with this: You simply left out the crucial matter, namely that you were present at the scene of a brutal senseless murder? You agree you've deliberately left that out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Well, nobody asked about that. Nobody insisted on it. So it was left out. Who said in any statement so and so killed someone?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And did you go on to say: "At about 0900 hours we got up. Sulejman Lujinovic came to us and asked if we knew what happened the night before. Dino and I were still lying in bed and asked him what happened. He replied that all the villagers had been killed that evening." Is that true? Did that happen or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, it's true. Between the 9th and the 10th, that night all the civilians were killed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no. Did you find yourself woken up by Mr. Lujinovic with that dreadful, shocking news?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No. We were already awake, but we didn't know all the civilians had been killed. We knew about Pero Maric but not the other civilians. And when they came and we saw those traces of blood, that's when they said that all the civilians had been killed. And Pero Maric was killed a day earlier, the day before, the 9th, the 10th, in the afternoon or, rather, at dusk.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you go on to say this: "Dino and I were still lying in bed and asked him what had happened. He replied that all the villagers had been killed that evening. The two of us got up and asked him for details. He told us that three men in uniform with their faces covered had come into the house where he was sleeping and in which the owners of the house had stayed and took the woman and her husband out of the house"? Now, did Mr. Lujinovic really tell you that or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No, I never said that. I just know that they told me that all the civilians had been killed that night in the village of Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: As for people going in with caps on their heads and taking out civilians and killing them, I didn't know that. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So how does it find its way into the statement that you gave to Dragan Mijokovic and signed yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Let me tell you. They never let you read those statements. They would just give us a piece of paper to sign and that was the end of it. That's how it was in Bosnia. You don't understand that. A man kills another man and suddenly he's innocent. There are a hundred witnesses and they all say that no murder took place, and then the man is acquitted. That's Bosnia for you. It's not the European Union. It's not the European Community. It's a lawless state run by people --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Witness D.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's a relatively new topic coming. I think I can do two more questions on this, but it's a matter for Your Honour. I think we've reached the time, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if you could save it for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That would be all right. I think the hearing for today is adjourned. Well, Witness, I have to warn you, as I did to the other witnesses, that while you are in The Hague you're still under the oath, so do not let anybody and do not talk to anybody about your testimony. You understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll see you tomorrow morning. The hearing for today is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 22nd day of February, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
